advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Replace verbatim rubric-prose substring/adjacency assertions with a structural-contract check or drive the reviewer's actual transient/durable classification behavior.
evidence: _assert_scope_then_safety asserts `_T10_SCOPE_CLAUSE in text` and `_T10_MAJOR_SAFETY_QUALIFIER in text` plus `text[scope_end:safety_start].strip() == ""` (adjacency)
The asserted strings are the verbatim rubric prose at src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_T10.md:10 and :12, consumed by an LLM reviewer at runtime — no machine parser branches on the exact wording
test_t10_rubric_co_locates_scope_and_major_safety_contract / test_t10_explain_and_generated_guide_render_scope_partition assert the same verbatim prose across .md, docs guide, and explain output
advisory.finding: The new T10 rubric/guide tests assert exact multi-sentence prose strings (_T10_SCOPE_CLAUSE, _T10_MAJOR_SAFETY_QUALIFIER) plus their adjacency/ordering in three artifacts (reviewer .md, docs guide, explain_criterion output). These strings are prose consumed by the LLM reviewer, not parsed by any non-human consumer, so the assertions are change-detectors: any behavior-preserving reword of the rubric breaks them, and they cannot detect a regression in what the reviewer actually flags for transient-vs-durable infra.
scenarios: An author rewords the scope-exclusion sentence without changing the reviewer's transient/durable behavior — all three tests fail despite no behavior regression
A genuine behavior regression (reviewer starts flagging in-scope transient experiments) leaves this exact-string prose intact — tests still pass

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Anchor the corpus-coverage check on stable case ids/expect labels (or structural fields) rather than substring-matching case note/input prose.
evidence: `_matching_case_ids` keeps a case only if `all(term in _normalized_case_text(case) for term in terms)` over tuples like `("loopback","teardown")` and `("wildcard","admin")`
Assertions `all(len(ids) == 1 ...)` couple the test to specific words appearing in each case's free-text note/input
advisory.finding: test_t10_eval_corpus_covers_each_pass_and_finding_boundary verifies coverage by substring-matching lowercased term tuples against each case's `note`+`input` prose (via _normalized_case_text). This asserts the corpus authoring text rather than any executable behavior, so it breaks on a benign reword of a case note/input even when the corpus still exercises the same boundary, and it does not verify the reviewer actually classifies those cases correctly.
scenarios: An author rephrases a pass-case note (e.g. drops the word 'teardown') without weakening the boundary the case covers — the term-match count drops and the test fails
Case notes are reworded during corpus tuning while the balanced 5/5 pass/finding structure is preserved
